title: gap:M0:L_rt_go_v0: M0's whole-header round trip dec_go(enc_sol(h)) = some(view(h)) at version 0 has no M3 law to pair with
outside: No catalog rule states a whole-record round trip. PAR's round_trip producer (P1) states one law per E1 inverse atom (encoder, getter, version): L_par_rt_enc_sol_BatchHeaderBytes_<F>_v0, 11 at version 0: ten of view's fields plus BlobCommitHash, which reads the blobVersionedHash slot. All of them are PROVED. None covers the slot enc_sol fills with a constant: SequencerSetVerifyHash, written as bytes32(0) whatever the header, a field M3's R_Header does not have. name: PAR_record_round_trip

basis.argument: An encoder enc into a byte record, and a decoder given as a family of getters {G} valid at version N, satisfy dec(enc(h)) = some(view_N(h)) iff every getter of the family returns, on enc(h), the value view_N gives its slot. The encoder fills each slot in one of two ways. From a record field F: PAR's round_trip law G(enc(h)) == Some(h.F) states it. With a constant c it writes whatever h is: the constant read-back law G(enc(h)) == Some(c) states it. The record law is the conjunction over the whole family at version N, under the version pin. It adds no premise, because a constant slot has no field on the encoder's record. Under mu, the source's Header maps to the record by forgetting the constant slots, dec_go maps to the getter family, and view maps to the getter tuple in view's order with each constant slot mapped to its constant. The source's own premise (M0: sequencerSetVerifyHash = 0) equates view's slot with c. So each B3 bridge is one implication, and it is refuted where the source lacks that premise. Getters outside view (BlobCommitHash) only add conjuncts on M3's side.
basis.obligation: Per instance, at version N: (1) every round_trip law L_par_rt_enc_sol_BatchHeaderBytes_<F>_vN of the family, decided PROVED (all are, today); (2) a constant read-back law for each constant slot, here L_par_rt_enc_sol_BatchHeaderBytes_SequencerSetVerifyHash_vN, stating BatchHeaderBytes_SequencerSetVerifyHash(enc_sol(pin_h(h))) == Some(32 zero bytes), decided PROVED; (3) coverage: every BatchHeaderBytes getter valid at version N has a component, checked against the extracted getter family, not against the laws that exist; (4) the record law, generated from (1)-(3) by the producer on a new catalog version and checked by Bend; (5) the mu amendment above, with the B3 bridge to M0's L_rt_go_vN decided on the compiled models.

title: A codec bug that misaligns an encoder and its decoder (an off-by-one offset, a wrong version guard) leaves no rule obligation stating their round trip
outside: PAR's round-trip and pinned cross-component obligations are instantiated from evidence atoms (E1 inverse atoms, the Go basis of G4) that the evidence pass computes from the layouts of the very code being checked; a misaligned pair has no such evidence, so the rule as instantiated states nothing about it and the defect is outside every obligation HOLON derives (whitepaper §5.1: obligations need evidence at least medium).

title: No rule's obligation covers the full set of Bun auto-loaded config files; GENV enumerates two exact names (bunfig.toml, .env) while bun also loads .env.local and .env.<NODE_ENV> from the checker's cwd.
outside: The eight rules (PAR, UNDO, NAT, SYM, FACT, SORT, DISCH, OWN) state obligations over the model and the code; none states the checker-environment hygiene obligation that GENV implements. GENV's safe-environment obligation is a gate check, not a rule, and it enumerates filenames rather than the class 'any file bun reads from the checker's working directory', so the enforcement is narrower than AGENTS.md rule 8's intent (which holon/consumers.py reads as .env*).

title: A codec bug that misaligns enc_sol with the BatchHeaderBytes getters at a version N (round 3's m08: storeParentBatchHash writes at offset 216; m06: a getter version guard that drops LastBlockNumber at v1) leaves no obligation stating the whole-record round trip dec_go(enc_sol(h)) = some(view_N(h)) that the bug breaks
outside: PAR states its per-field round trips and pinned cross-component laws only where the evidence pass finds the encoder's and the getter's layouts agreeing (E1 inverse atoms, G4's Go basis), and no rule states the round trip of the whole record at version N. Under m08 the derivation drops L_par_rt_enc_sol_BatchHeaderBytes_ParentBatchHash_v0, _v1 and _v2 and the three enc_sol _pinned laws; under m06 it drops both LastBlockNumber_v1 round trips; neither adds a law (audit/rounds/M3/round3/a1_m08.json and a1_m06.json: derivation.added is empty). A1's 'detected' is only the diff against the committed laws, so on code that had the bug from its first extraction the misalignment is outside every obligation.
notes: Filed by the queue runner (lead triage) on F-M3-10's own evidence, as the part of RG-M3-04 that the candidate's drafted obligation closes. m08: clause (3) (coverage, checked against the extracted getter family, not against the laws that exist) fails on the missing ParentBatchHash component at v0-v2, so the record law is obstructed rather than silently dropped; a record law stated for the engines, and its B3 bridge to M0's L_rt_go_vN (5), would be refuted. m06: the getter family at v1 loses LastBlockNumber, and the bridge (5), whose view_1 has lastBlockNumber, is refuted. This is a reading of an unimplemented candidate, not a run: the implementing iteration should preregister m08 and m06 as caught (refuted or obstructed), not dropped, which tests this triage. RG-M3-04 (candidate null) keeps the rest of F-M3-10: m05 (the block-context carrier, with no M0 bridge), m07 (the Go encoders, inside the candidate only if its producer covers every encoder into the carrier, which its argument allows and its obligation does not say) and the A1 driver's reporting of a dropped PROVED law as detection.

title: PAR's round-trip obligation exists only for an encoder/decoder pair whose cells align, so a misaligned decoder (the defect) removes the obligation it should falsify
outside: PAR states round trips for evidenced pairs only (Appendix E basis: evidenced pairs), and the evidence that pairs an encoder with a decoder is the E1 alignment of the decoder's reads with the encoder's writes; a decoder of the same carrier and field whose reads are shifted has no evidenced pair, so no rule's obligation states its round trip
